title: Design System: Agent Connect Gateway Authorization

display.purpose: One decisive heading for the current owner task.

title.purpose: Groups profiles, authority, and operational access.

label.purpose: Buttons, fields, metadata, and explicit statuses.

shadows.name: authorization-plate
shadows.purpose: The sole desktop lift, separating the owner task from the cool page field.

motion.name: state-response
motion.purpose: Quiet hover feedback for buttons and authorization choices; omitted when reduced motion is preferred.

components.name: Agent Connect Wordmark
components.description: The shared Canvas identity: three circles map application, gateway, and agent before the Agent Connect name.
components.css: .ds-wordmark { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.65rem; color: oklch(0.2 0.018 250); font: 760 1rem/1.5 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.025em; } .ds-wordmark > span { display: inline-flex; gap: 0.19rem; } .ds-wordmark i { width: 0.44rem; height: 0.44rem; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-wordmark i:nth-child(1) { background: oklch(0.56 0.16 32.1); } .ds-wordmark i:nth-child(2) { background: oklch(0.43 0.09 190); } .ds-wordmark i:nth-child(3) { background: oklch(0.52 0.15 275); }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Affirmative owner actions such as Continue, Allow access, and Review request.
components.css: .ds-button-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 3rem; padding: 0.65rem 1rem; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 0.625rem; background: oklch(0.2 0.018 250); color: oklch(1 0 0); font: 700 1rem/1.5 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.16s ease-out; } .ds-button-primary:hover { background: oklch(0.27 0.022 250); } .ds-button-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid oklch(0.52 0.15 275); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A legible non-destructive alternative, most often Cancel.
components.css: .ds-button-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 3rem; padding: 0.65rem 1rem; border: 1px solid oklch(0.7 0.018 250); border-radius: 0.625rem; background: oklch(1 0 0); color: oklch(0.2 0.018 250); font: 700 1rem/1.5 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-button-secondary:hover { background: oklch(0.972 0.006 250); } .ds-button-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid oklch(0.52 0.15 275); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Explicit revocation action with restrained destructive color.
components.css: .ds-button-danger { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 3rem; padding: 0.65rem 1rem; border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklch, oklch(0.5 0.18 25) 45%, white); border-radius: 0.625rem; background: white; color: oklch(0.5 0.18 25); font: 700 1rem/1.5 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-button-danger:hover { background: oklch(0.96 0.03 25); } .ds-button-danger:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid oklch(0.52 0.15 275); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Enrollment Field
components.description: A plainly labeled owner credential field with persistent recovery guidance.
components.css: .ds-field { display: grid; gap: 0.45rem; color: oklch(0.2 0.018 250); font: 700 1rem/1.5 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-field input { width: 100%; min-height: 3rem; padding: 0.72rem 0.8rem; border: 1px solid oklch(0.7 0.018 250); border-radius: 0.625rem; background: white; color: oklch(0.2 0.018 250); font: 400 1rem/1.5 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; caret-color: oklch(0.43 0.09 190); } .ds-field input:hover { border-color: oklch(0.43 0.09 190); } .ds-field input:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid oklch(0.52 0.15 275); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-field small { color: oklch(0.46 0.018 250); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 400; }

components.name: Authorization Plate
components.description: The stable task shell shared by authentication, consent, problems, and owner access management.
components.html:
reader.exampleAuthorization request

Review access

Choose the restricted profile this application may use.
components.css: .ds-plate { width: min(100%, 32rem); overflow: hidden; border-radius: 0.875rem; background: white; color: oklch(0.2 0.018 250); box-shadow: 0 0.5rem 1.8rem oklch(0.2 0.018 250 / 0.1); font: 400 1rem/1.5 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-plate header, .ds-plate > div { padding: clamp(1.25rem, 4vw, 2rem); } .ds-plate header { display: grid; border-bottom: 1px solid oklch(0.85 0.012 250); } .ds-plate header span, .ds-plate p { color: oklch(0.46 0.018 250); } .ds-plate h2 { margin: 0; font-size: clamp(1.55rem, 5vw, 2rem); line-height: 1.18; letter-spacing: -0.025em; } .ds-plate p { margin: 0.75rem 0 0; } @media (max-width: 560px) { .ds-plate { width: 100%; border-radius: 0; box-shadow: none; } }

components.name: Restricted Profile Choice
components.description: A full-row radio target that names the profile and its native authority.
components.css: .ds-choice { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr; gap: 0.1rem 0.75rem; padding: 0.9rem; border: 1px solid oklch(0.85 0.012 250); border-radius: 0.625rem; color: oklch(0.2 0.018 250); font: 400 1rem/1.5 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-choice input { grid-row: 1 / 4; margin-top: 0.3rem; accent-color: oklch(0.43 0.09 190); } .ds-choice strong, .ds-choice span, .ds-choice small { grid-column: 2; } .ds-choice span { color: oklch(0.46 0.018 250); } .ds-choice:hover { border-color: oklch(0.7 0.018 250); background: oklch(0.972 0.006 250); } .ds-choice:has(input:checked) { border-color: oklch(0.43 0.09 190); background: oklch(0.95 0.025 190); } .ds-choice:has(input:focus-visible) { outline: 3px solid oklch(0.52 0.15 275); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Active Status
components.description: A compact status word whose dot reinforces but never replaces its meaning.
components.css: .ds-status-active { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.4rem; color: oklch(0.48 0.12 150); font: 750 0.8rem/1.5 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-status-active::before { content: ""; width: 0.48rem; height: 0.48rem; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; }

narrative.overview:
Agent Connect uses the familiar topology of a modern identity-provider flow without borrowing a vendor's identity or implying that familiarity is proof of security. A cool work surface holds one crisp authorization plate whose stable brand, reading order, and action placement carry authentication, consent, errors, and access management. Application context appears inside the plate only when a requesting application is in scope. The three-circle Canvas wordmark and its actor palette are the shared Agent Connect identity.

The system is calm, candid, and capable. It favors workhorse type, plain authority language, generous breathing room, and restrained state color over decorative security imagery or dashboard density. On narrow screens, the plate becomes the page while preserving the same order and explicit owner choices.
keyCharacteristics: One centered authorization plate on wide screens and one full-width task surface on phones.
Workbench-ink hierarchy, quiet cool neutrals, and actor colors inherited from the Canvas application.
Authority details disclosed progressively without hiding application identity or owner choices.
Status expressed with wording as well as restrained color.

rules.name: The Actor Color Rule
rules.body: Coral means application, teal means gateway boundary, and periwinkle means agent or focus. Primary decisions remain workbench ink; semantic states keep their own restrained colors.

rules.name: The Words Carry Status Rule
rules.body: Color may reinforce state, but active, pending, expired, revoked, and problem states must remain understandable from their text.

rules.name: The Workhorse Type Rule
rules.body: Use one native sans-serif family and let content hierarchy—not typographic novelty—carry the authorization flow.

rules.name: The Stable Reading Order Rule
rules.body: Responsive changes may alter width, padding, and columns, but never reorder application identity, the current task, authority details, and owner actions.

rules.name: The One Lift Rule
rules.body: Only the desktop authorization plate is elevated; hierarchy inside it comes from spacing, rules, and tonal fills.

rules.name: The Nested Corner Rule
rules.body: Corners tighten as elements nest: plate, then choice, then control. Do not introduce ornamental pills or mixed corner styles.

dos: Do preserve the same shell and action placement across owner authentication, consent, problems, and access management; include the context header only for application-scoped requests.
Do name the requesting application before asking the owner to authenticate or authorize.
Do keep application tools visibly distinct from native capabilities and selected restricted profiles.
Do provide explicit keyboard focus, touch-sized controls, reduced-motion behavior, and text alongside every semantic color.
Do let mobile become a full-width task surface while preserving the desktop reading order.
donts: Don't use visual familiarity, color, or a polished plate as evidence of security; the copy must state actual authority and boundaries.
Don't add decorative security imagery, trust scores, ornamental dashboards, or unexplained protocol language.
Don't hide cancel or revocation behind low-contrast links, menus, or color-only warnings.
Don't introduce a second affirmative accent, stacked card shadows, pill-shaped controls, or a decorative display face.
